title: World War Three is NOT coming, BUT . . .
summary: A historian argues World War 3 is not coming: today's conflicts resemble the pre-1914 imperial 'armed peace' of endless small wars, not the two world wars.

assertions.quote: Because World War III never comes.
It does not declare the start of World War III.
how today's global conflicts do not resemble two brief periods of war in the 20th century

verdicts.note: Multipolar rivalry and regional powder kegs echo 1914, but nuclear deterrence and the absence of mobilisation-driven war plans make the analogy loose.

assertions.quote: They resemble an earlier period of worldwide imperial violence from 1500 to 1914, which became a sprawling regime of armed peace.

verdicts.note: An interpretive framework for current conflicts, not a checkable fact.

assertions.quote: Following our definition and within this time span, the Great War, World War I, was actually World War VII.

verdicts.note: Under definitions like Hamilton and Herwig's (five or more major powers, fighting on two or more continents), several 17th- and 18th-century wars qualify.

assertions.quote: the USA state's refusal to renounce the perpetual threat of limited nuclear first strike

verdicts.note: No US nuclear posture review has adopted a no-first-use policy.
SIPRI cites the 2018 US Nuclear Posture Review: the US would consider a nuclear response to 'significant non-nuclear strategic attacks', which is a first-use option.

assertions.quote: is a slow-moving global rebellion against the USA's post-1945 dominion

verdicts.note: An interpretive framing of disparate conflicts.
UCDP says a widening array of states challenge norms upheld by US hegemony, but also that the US itself is turning against that order and that the conflicts are concentrated in a few countries.
